# 03 Animate every element carrying a target id

## Outcome

A timeline target's effect classes land on **every** element in the SVG carrying that
`data-siren-id`, not just the first one in document order.

## Why this ticket exists

`applyClassState` resolves a target with
`svg.querySelector('[data-siren-id="${targetId}"]')`. That has been correct by accident: flowchart
nodes and edges, and class-diagram classes, relationships, namespaces and notes are each drawn as
exactly one element, so first-match and all-matches agree.

They stop agreeing at the sequence diagram. `renderSequenceToSVG` already tags participants,
lifelines, box groupings, control-flow blocks, messages and destroy marks with `data-siren-id`, and
a declared, never-destroyed participant is drawn **twice** — once at the top row, once at the
bottom (`buildParticipant` takes `top` as a parameter for exactly that reason) — plus its lifeline,
plus possibly a destroy mark. One id, up to four elements. Wire the timeline to a sequence diagram
today and `highlight A outline` lights the top box and leaves the lifeline and bottom box alone.

The underlying question is what a timeline target *is*, and nobody has answered it: the code
currently answers "whichever element is first", which is not a decision anyone made. See ADR-0009,
written by this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] With two elements sharing one `data-siren-id`, `next()` applies the step's effect class to
  both.
- [x] `prev()` and `reset()` clear and restore the classes on both — the controller's canonical
  class state is recomputed per step, so a second element must not be able to keep a stale class.
- [x] Initial `siren-pending` for a target with an `enter` action is set on both. **Reworded
  during implementation**: setting the initial `siren-pending` is the renderer's job, not the
  controller's — the controller only clears and restores it. Tested as "reset restores
  `siren-pending` on every element carrying the id".
- [x] A target matching no element is still skipped silently, exactly as today.
- [x] Non-effect classes on every matched element are left alone (`siren-participant`,
  `siren-lifeline`, ...), as the existing `isEffectClass` guard already guarantees for one element.
- [x] `docs/adr/0009-*.md` records the decision: a timeline target is an id, and it reaches every
  element carrying it. State the rejected alternative (per-element ids such as `A:lifeline`,
  `A:bottom`) and why: it makes a layout detail into an id convention authors must learn.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md`'s `Timeline target` entry states the one-id-many-elements rule.
- [x] All 12 existing controller tests pass unchanged — no current diagram kind draws one id twice,
  so this must be a pure widening.

## Test seam

`createAnimationController(svg, timeline)`. It already accepts the SVG as a parameter, so the test
builds one directly with two elements sharing an id. Note honestly that no shipped document
produces that shape *and* animates yet: this ticket is observable only at this seam until the
sequence-animation board lands.
